fn render(ref mut dev: dyn Device, ref mut game: Game) -> Result[void, GpuError]:
    started = dev.begin_frame()
    match owns started:
        Some(frame):
            minimap = dev.create_texture(game.minimap_desc())?
            mask = dev.create_texture(game.mask_desc())?      # fails: `frame` is abandoned, `minimap` lives on
            draw_minimap(ref mut frame, minimap, mask)
            dev.end_frame(owns frame)
            dev.destroy(minimap)
            dev.destroy(mask)
        None:
            pass
    return Ok(())

Handles are Copy names (GPU-1), so `minimap` stays alive until the device ends (other case 13, open risk 6). When the mask allocation keeps failing (out of GPU memory), every frame leaks one more minimap texture, which makes the out-of-memory error permanent. In C the `goto cleanup` would destroy it. The design states this as accepted behaviour, not as a gap.
holes.fix_hint: Add an owning Texture/Buffer type (not Copy; its end calls destroy through the same inferred device tie) whose Copy handle is a view of it, so rule 1 covers GPU objects. Ask it with this group, because it is DRP-9 rule 1 applied to GPU objects, not a separate library nicety.

holes.program:
fn run(ref mut dev: dyn Device, ref mut game: Game):
    pending: Option[Frame] = None
    while game.running:
        pending = dev.begin_frame()          # a frame from the round before may still be held here
        game.update(1.0 / 60.0)
        if game.ready:
            match owns mem.take(ref mut pending):
                Some(frame):
                    draw_world(ref mut frame, game)
                    dev.end_frame(owns frame)
                None:
                    pass
holes.what_goes_wrong: OWN-5 evaluates the new value, then drops the old one. In a round where game.ready was false, line 4 therefore begins frame N+1 while frame N is still open, and only then abandons N. GPU-2, even as changed, never says whether a device may have two frames open. With a two-image swapchain and one frame in flight, the acquire for N+1 waits for the image that N's abandon gives back only afterwards. That is a hang, and in Vulkan it is invalid usage (an infinite-timeout acquire with too many images held). The design's other case 5 checks OWN-5 and DRP-8 but not this order.
holes.fix_hint: Decide it in GPU-2: begin_frame while another frame of the same device is open returns None (no image is free). The replacement then gives None, N is abandoned, the round is skipped and the next begin_frame works. Alternatively, state how many frames may be open at once. Either way, name OWN-5's order in the case.

holes.what_goes_wrong: The design ties the Frame to the device with a sharedref mut link, so by verdict 164 a Frame, and any CommandList that views it, is neither Send nor ThreadShared. Scoped tasks reach it only through the caller's variable, and one `ref mut frame` cannot go to several tasks (BRW-1), so one core records the whole scene. C on Vulkan or D3D12 records secondary command buffers on N threads with per-thread pools, which is how renderers scale draw submission. The design's open risk 4 covers moving frames between threads but not this loss. It is a ceiling that the choice of link puts in.
holes.fix_hint: Keep verdict 164 and the tie, and let the frame lend disjoint command lists that hold no device link: `frame.command_lists(n)` split like MutSpan.split_at, each holding only its own recording, so each is Send. The lists are tied to the frame by region (LT-1) and put their recordings back into the frame when they end (GPU-13 already says so). Only the frame keeps the device link.

engineering.notes:
P23 engineering review. Read in full: owner-bar.md, brief.md, OWNER-DIRECTION.md, phase1-groups.json (all 28 principles), phase2 J7-19, phase3 K60 (it has no notes, conflicts or recommendation changes for this item), Annex D (p22), VII.1-VII.8 (OWN, BRW, LT-1/1a/4/45/46/47/48, DRP-1 to 8), RC-7, TYP-45, IV.4, IV.9, CLS-7a/9/9a, CORO-6/7, CTL-8, GRM-7, PAN-1, STD-22/24, THR-5/6/15, JOB-2, ARN-1/6, FFI-23, and JOB.md verdicts 56 to 62, 140 and 164 to 166.

What holds:
- The ordinary game loop is unchanged character for character.
- The J7-19 outcome is right, and option A is the right choice over B, C and D.
- DRP-8 makes the hidden end visible to the lock and walk rules (consistent with P05).
- No forget or `discard self` comes back (verdict 58).
- Effects through dyn abandon_frame reach @noalloc/@nopanic callers (consistent with P14).

The medium holes are about the tie and the protocol, not about the end law itself:
1. BRW-1's 'a ref mut name is alone, a link of the same type included' refuses the frame's link changing the device while `ref mut dev` is used. Only LT-4 (managers) carves this out, and the design adds a second per-type sentence (GPU-2) instead of one rule in LT-46/BRW-1.
2. The tie needs `sharedref mut dyn Device`, which TYP-45/IV.9 do not give (P12's open form).
3. A Renderer class owning its device and its in-progress frame compiles today and has no spelling under the rule (LT-45 plus CLS-9a). The design's E3063 help 'keep the device with it' does not compile.
4. The public abandon_frame hook lets a program abandon and then submit (undefined), and it is a second spelling of skipping a frame.
5. Once-ness rests on each Device implementer taking the work out of a std type with private fields.
6. History/Ring own GPU resources but give nothing back, and Copy handles leak on `?` until the device ends.
7. OWN-5's order begins a new frame before abandoning the held one; GPU-2 does not say whether two frames may be open, and a two-image swapchain can hang.
8. Verdict 164 applied to the chosen link closes parallel command recording, which C/Vulkan does routinely.
9. A BufWriter's failed drop write is silent data loss with Ok returned.

Every fix keeps verdicts 56/57/58/69/140/164 and needs no new word in ordinary code. Holes 1 and 3 change BRW-1/LT-46 and LT-45, so they are owner questions. Present P23 after P12 (sharedref mut dyn I) and next to P11 (exists as plus owns, which decides whether the ordinary loop can be written as `if dev.begin_frame() exists as frame:`).

design.rule: Ending a value means giving back. A value ends by its type's `drop` on every way out of its scope (the block's end, `return`, `?`, `break`, `continue`). It also ends that way when it is overwritten or cleared, handed to `mem.drop`, ended with whatever owns it, or left in a generator that is dropped while suspended. Every standard type's end does three things. (1) It gives back everything the value still holds, once. (2) It keeps what the value's calls have already done. It discards work that only the type's finishing call makes real, and leaves what that work would have changed as it was. (3) It cannot fail or stop the program, and no failure goes unseen. A step of the end that can fail is also a call that returns its Result. The compiler finds that step in the drop's body. If the value ends on a path that does not leave by an error, and the last call that changed it on that path was not that step, the Result is unused: W2190 at the line where the value ends. A finishing call is a method of the value's own type that takes the value over (`frame.present()`, a transaction's `commit()`). It hands the pending work, which is a value of its own, to the step that makes it real. So the work is made real or discarded exactly once, by its one owner, with no hook and no extra flag. A value whose end gives back to a provider is made by a method of that provider, so it points into it and never outlives it. It points in through a view where the provider is not otherwise used meanwhile. Where the program goes on using the provider, it holds a kept `sharedref mut` link made from the provider's name; that name is then one of the link's holders. A class that keeps both the provider and the value says `from` the provider's field, and that field is then never replaced. For J7-19: the `?` abandons the frame. Nothing is shown, and its image goes back to the device. Its recording, its memory and the objects made through it are given back, and the next `begin_frame` works.
design.spec_text:
ADDS [DRP-9], [GPU-13] and [GPU-14]. CHANGES [LT-46] (the holders of a `sharedref mut` link), [LT-45] (a class that keeps a provider and what it made), [LT-4] and [BRW-22] (each now cites [LT-46]), [STD-22], the W2190 row of [ERR-5], the Annex D listing, [GPU-2], [GPU-3], [GPU-4], [GPU-6] and [GPU-8]. D.1's example is unchanged. [DRP-6], [THR-5], [JOB-2], [ARN-6], [FFI-23], [THR-15] and "Dropping a JoinHandle detaches" are unchanged; each is an instance of [DRP-9]. It needs P12's `sharedref mut dyn I` and P16's rule for elements written by one task each.

* `[DRP-9]` *(new in 0.9.15)* **Ending a value gives back.** A value ends by its type's `drop` (`[DRP-1]`) in these cases:
  - on every way out of its owner's scope: the block's end, `return`, `?`, `break` and `continue` (`[CTL-8]`);
  - when its owner is overwritten or cleared (`[OWN-5]`);
  - when it is handed to `mem.drop` (`[OWN-6]`);
  - at the end of the statement that made it as a temporary (`[DRP-3]`);
  - when what owns it ends: a container, a value, a function value's state, or the last `shares` owner (`[DRP-2]`, `[DRP-6]`, `[CLO-10]`, `[RC-1]`);
  - when a suspended generator holding it is dropped (`[CORO-7]`).

  A value handed to C (`[OWN-12]`) has not ended: C holds it, and it ends by its type's end when C gives it back. Every standard-library type's end does three things, and the type's own rule says what each one is for it:
  1. **It gives back everything the value still holds**, once: memory to its manager, a lock unlocked, a file closed, an image to its device, a count subtracted (`[DRP-6]`), C's hold on a callback released (`[FFI-23]`).
  2. **It keeps what is done and discards what is pending.** What the value's calls have done stays done: bytes a `write` accepted reach the file (`[STD-22]`), changes made under a guard stay, a task started in a scope runs to its end (`[THR-5]`), and commands recorded in a command list stay in its frame (`[GPU-13]`). Some work the type makes real only in its **finishing call**, a method of the value's own type that takes the value over (`frame.present()`, a library's `fn commit() owns this -> Result[void, DbError]`). That work is pending until that call. An end without the call discards the work and leaves what it would have changed as it was.
  3. **It cannot fail and does not stop the program, and no failure goes unseen.** A step of an end that can fail is also a call that returns its `Result`. In the type's `drop`, a call of one of the type's own methods that returns a `Result` (a `BufWriter`'s `this.flush()`) is such a step; the compiler reads it from the `drop`'s body. Take a path that does not leave by `?` or by a `return` of an `Err`. If the value may end on it by making that step, and the last call on that path that changed the value was not that step, the step's `Result` is unused: `W2190` (`[ERR-5]`) at the line where the value ends ("`w` ends here and writes the bytes it may hold, and a failure there cannot be reported; to hear it, write `w.flush()?` above line 9"). When such a step fails at the end itself, what it was doing is lost, and rules 1 and 2 still hold for the rest. On an error path the program is already reporting a failure.

  **A finishing call hands the pending work over.** The value holds the pending work as a value of its own (a `Frame`'s work, `[GPU-14]`), or marks it in a field (`open: bool`). The finishing call takes it out (`mem.take`, `[OWN-6]`) and makes it real, so the end that runs at the call's end finds nothing pending. The work is made real or discarded exactly once, by its one owner (`[OWN-1]`). There is no hook a program can call and no flag beyond the `Option` that holds the work, and no value ends without its `drop` (`[OWN-2]`).

  **A value whose end gives back to a provider in the program is made by a method of that provider, so it points into it** (`[LT-1]`) and lives no longer than it (`E3063`). It does so in one of two ways:
  - through a view, where the provider is not otherwise used while the value lives: a guard and its lock, a `ScopedArena` and its arena (`[ARN-6]`), a command list and its frame (`[GPU-13]`);
  - through a kept `sharedref mut` link made from the provider's name, where the program goes on using the provider (`[LT-46]`): a value made in a memory manager's instance (`[LT-4]`), and a `Frame`, `Ring` or `History` and its device.

  A panic and `process.exit` leave no scope. The process ends with no `drop` run (`[PAN-1]`, `[STD-24]`), and the operating system takes back what the process held. A program's own `drop` SHOULD follow rules 1 to 3; rule 3's `W2190` reads its body the same way.

* `[LT-46]` *(changed in 0.9.15)*, under `sharedref mut T`, one paragraph added. A link made from a name makes that name one of the link's holders while the link lives. The link may be written (`sharedref mut p`) or held in a value that a method of `p` made (`[LT-1]`). An owner or a `ref mut` name and the links made from it may then each change the object, and `[BRW-1]`'s "a `ref mut` name is alone" holds against every other name. A call may be given such a `ref mut` name together with a value that holds one of its links (`upload(ref mut dev, ref mut frame)`). Inside the call the parameter is a holder too. For such calls the parameter is compiled without noalias, in a copy of the function, as `[BRW-11]`'s exception 1 makes one (`[BRW-22]`). `[LT-4]`'s link to a manager's instance is such a link, and `[LT-4]` cites this paragraph instead of stating it.

* `[LT-45]` *(changed in 0.9.15)*, one paragraph added after "`from static`". A view field whose views are all kept `sharedref mut` links (a `Frame`, `[GPU-2]`) may instead say `from <field>`, naming a field declared before it whose value lives in a block of its own (an `owns T`, a class object, a `String`, an `Array`), `let` or not. Such a link stays valid while its object changes; views through it end at a reshape (`[BRW-17]`). Only replacing that field, or handing it over, would leave the link pointing at nothing. So:
  - that field is never replaced or handed over after `init` (`E2104`: "`this.dev` is replaced here, and `pending` points into it (`from dev`, line 3); to use another device, make another `Renderer`");
  - its object is changed through it and through the links, as `[LT-46]` lets every holder do;
  - it ends after the view field (`[DRP-2]`), so a `drop` that reaches it through a link still finds it (`[DRP-7]`).

* `[STD-22]` *(changed in 0.9.15)* … A `File` closes when dropped; the bytes its `write` calls took are with the operating system. `BufReader` and `BufWriter` buffer. A `BufWriter`'s `drop` writes what it holds with `this.flush()` and then ends what it wraps. So a `BufWriter` that ends after a `write` with no `w.flush()` since, on a path that does not leave by an error, is `W2190` (`[DRP-9]` rule 3). Writing `w.flush()?` above that line hands a failure to the caller.

* `[ERR-5]`, the `W2190` row of the code table: "unused `Result`, including `check_disjoint`'s and that of a step an end makes (`[DRP-9]` rule 3)".

* Annex D, the listing:
```ember,fragment
interface Device:
    fn begin_frame() -> Result[Option[Frame], GpuError]   # None: no frame this time
    fn create_texture(desc: TextureDesc) -> Result[TextureHandle, GpuError]
    fn create_buffer(desc: BufferDesc) -> Result[BufferHandle, GpuError]
    fn destroy(h: TextureHandle)                          # physical destruction is deferred
    fn frames_in_flight() -> int

interface FrameWork:                                      # written by a Device implementer: one frame's work on the device
    fn submit() owns this -> Result[void, GpuError]       # submits what was recorded and shows the image
                                                          # its drop gives the image back unshown and discards the recording
```

* `[GPU-2]` *(changed in 0.9.15)* `device.begin_frame() -> Result[Option[Frame], GpuError]`. `Ok(None)` is normal: a minimised window, or a frame of this device still open (`[GPU-14]`). `Err` is a lost device.
  - A `Frame` has one owner and is not `Copy`. It holds a kept `sharedref mut` link made from its device (`[LT-46]`), so it lives no longer than the device (`E3063`), while the program goes on using the device. A class that keeps both writes the frame's field `from` the device's field (`[LT-45]`).
  - `frame.present() -> Result[void, GpuError]` is the frame's finishing call (`[DRP-9]`). It takes the frame over (the name `frame` ends, `[FN-4]`), hands the frame's work to `submit`, and shows the image. `Err` is a lost device or a failed present, and the device is then in the state an abandoned frame leaves it in. Presenting a frame twice, or after it ended, is refused when compiling (`E3040`). A frame presents itself, so no device is ever given another device's frame.
  - **A `Frame` that ends any other way is abandoned**: an early `return` or `?`, a `break` or `continue`, `mem.drop(owns frame)`, its holder overwritten or cleared, or a suspended generator holding it dropped. Its work ends (`[GPU-14]`). After that:
    - nothing recorded in the frame reaches the GPU, so what that work would have written keeps its contents, while what the CPU wrote during the frame (through a mapping, by an upload) stays (`[DRP-9]` rule 2);
    - its image goes back to the device unshown, and the window keeps the last frame shown;
    - its transient memory, and the objects made through it, are given back (`[GPU-3]`);
    - no resource is in flight because of it (`[GPU-4]`), and `frames_in_flight()`, `Ring` and `History` count only presented frames;
    - what was created or destroyed through the device during the frame stays created or destroyed, and a destruction waits only for the frames that were presented (`[GPU-6]`);
    - the device's next `begin_frame` works as usual, or gives `Err` if the device was lost in the meantime.

* `[GPU-3]` *(changed in 0.9.15)* `frame.arena()` … so nothing made in it outlives the frame. `frame.create_texture(desc)` and `frame.create_buffer(desc)` make GPU objects that belong to the frame. They are destroyed when the frame ends: after the GPU has finished the frame if it was presented (`[GPU-6]`), at once if it was abandoned. Their handles are stale afterwards (`[GPU-1]`).

* `[GPU-4]` *(changed in 0.9.15)* … `Ring[T, N]` holds one resource per frame in flight (`ring.current(frame)`). A `Ring` is made from a device and holds a kept link made from it, as a `Frame` does (`[GPU-2]`); its end destroys what it holds (`[GPU-6]`).

* `[GPU-6]` *(changed in 0.9.15)* `device.destroy(h)` invalidates the handle at once and destroys the object after the GPU has finished the frames that may use it. Ending the device waits for the GPU, flushes every retirement list, and destroys every object whose handle is still live (`[DRP-9]` rule 1); `debug` reports each of those as leaked (`[GPU-7]`). No `Frame`, `Ring` or `History` of the device is still alive at that point (`E3063`).

* `[GPU-8]` *(changed in 0.9.15)* `History[T]` owns the per-frame copies of a temporal resource (`gpu.History[TextureHandle].new(ref mut device, desc, count=2)`). It holds a kept link made from the device, as a `Frame` does, and its end destroys its copies (`[GPU-6]`). It gives `(prev, cur)` for each presented frame, and forbids reads of `cur` and writes of `prev` within a frame.

* `[GPU-13]` *(new in 0.9.15)* **Command lists.**
  - `frame.command_list()` gives a `CommandList` that records into a part of the frame of its own (`from` that part, `[LT-1a]`), not into the whole frame. While the list lives, the rest of the frame is used as usual (`frame.arena()`, `frame.create_texture(...)`, `ring.current(frame)`), because those reach other parts (`[BRW-4]`, `[BRW-10]`, `[LT-35]`).
  - `frame.command_lists(n)` gives `n` lists at once, disjoint as the views `chunks_mut` gives (`[SPN-4]`). Scoped tasks may then record one list each, reaching the frame where it is (verdict 164, `[THR-11]`): `lists = frame.command_lists(chunks.len())`, then in `with scope = thread.scope():` the loop `for i in 0..chunks.len():` with `scope.spawn(owns fn() copy of i: record_chunk(ref mut lists[i], chunks[i]))`. The frame submits the recordings in the order the lists were given.
  - Presenting the frame before a list's last use is refused when compiling.
  - A list's end, on every path, closes what it left open (`end_render_pass()` for an open pass), so the frame's recording is always complete. Whether that recording is shown is the frame's to decide (`[GPU-2]`).

* `[GPU-14]` *(new in 0.9.15)* **What a device implementer gives a frame.**
  - An implementer's `begin_frame` makes the frame with `Frame.new(sharedref mut this, owns work)`, where `work` is a value of the implementer's own type implementing `FrameWork`. Its `submit()` takes it over, submits what was recorded and shows the image. Its `drop` gives the image back unshown and discards the recording. A `submit` that fails leaves the device as that `drop` does.
  - The frame owns its work. `frame.present()` hands the work to `submit`, and every other end of the frame ends it, so a frame is submitted or abandoned exactly once, by the work's one owner (`[OWN-1]`, `[DRP-9]`).
  - No program calls either one directly: `Device` has no such method, and a frame's work is reached only through its frame.
  - A device has at most one open frame. While a frame's work is out, the device's `begin_frame` gives `Ok(None)`, never waiting for an image. In `debug` the device reports this once, naming the line that began the open frame.
  - A device lost while a frame is being abandoned is reported by its next `begin_frame`.

answers.answer: The rule decides it. An early exit by `?` ends `frame` by its drop, and a Frame that ends without its finishing call `frame.present()` is abandoned (GPU-2 under DRP-9 rule 2). The frame owns its device work (GPU-14), so ending the frame ends that work. The work's drop discards the recording and gives the swapchain image back unshown. The frame's memory, and anything made through the frame, are given back (GPU-3). Every resource the frame recorded keeps the contents and access state it had before the frame, and the device is ready for the next begin_frame. The error goes back to the caller as the program says. Nothing stops the program and nothing undefined happens. The work is submitted or abandoned exactly once, because it has one owner; there is no hook a program could call twice. The program is written with `match owns` because whether a name opened by `exists as` from a temporary may be handed over is P11's question; the outcome is the same in either spelling. `begin_frame()?` and `present()?` are the two places where a lost device is now heard (GPU-2).
answers.code:
from std.gpu import Device, Frame, GpuError, TextureDesc, TextureHandle

fn draw_sky(ref mut frame: Frame, sky: TextureHandle):
    pass                                             # records the sky pass

fn render(ref mut dev: dyn Device, desc: TextureDesc) -> Result[void, GpuError]:
    started = dev.begin_frame()?                     # acquires a swapchain image, opens a recording
    match owns started:
        Some(frame):
            sky = dev.create_texture(desc)?          # on an error, `?` returns: `frame` ends here, abandoned
            draw_sky(ref mut frame, sky)
            frame.present()?                         # submits and shows; `frame` ends here with its work taken
        None:
            pass                                     # a minimised window: no frame this time
    return Ok(())
answers.outcome: Compiles. When create_texture fails, render returns that error, and `frame` ends at the `?` line. Its work's drop discards the recording and gives the image back unshown, its arena is freed, and nothing it recorded is in flight. The window keeps the last frame shown, and the next dev.begin_frame() works as usual. When create_texture succeeds, frame.present() hands the work to the device's submit and shows the image; the frame ends at present's end and finds no work left. A lost device is an Err from begin_frame or present, which `?` returns.

other_cases.case: A command list left inside a render pass: `with cmd = frame.command_list():`, then `cmd.begin_render_pass(...)`, then a `continue` in a loop over meshes before `cmd.end_render_pass()`, and `frame.present()?` later.
other_cases.settled: GPU-13 under DRP-9 rule 2. The list's end records end_render_pass for the open pass, so the frame's recording is complete. The draws recorded before the exit are shown at present; abandoning the frame would discard them.

other_cases.case: Per-draw data from the frame while a list records: `inst = instances.current(frame)` and `frame.arena()` inside `with cmd = frame.command_list():`.
other_cases.settled: Compiles (GPU-13). The list views a part of the frame of its own. ring.current reads the frame's number and arena() reaches its arena, which are other parts (BRW-4, BRW-10, LT-35).

other_cases.case: `frame.present()` while a command list of that frame is still used.
other_cases.settled: Refused when compiling: a frame is not handed over while a view of it is used. The help moves present below the list's last use.

other_cases.case: A Frame kept past its device: returned from a function that does not return the device, or kept in an object that outlives the `ref mut dev` it came from.
other_cases.settled: E3063, because the frame holds a link made from the device. The help gives lines that compile: present the frame in this function (`frame.present()?` above line 12), or keep the device and the frame in one class (next case).

other_cases.case: A renderer class that begins in one method and presents in another. `class Renderer:` has `dev: owns dyn Device` and `pending: Option[Frame] from dev = None`. `fn begin_drawing() -> Result[void, GpuError]:` does `this.pending = this.dev.begin_frame()?` and `return Ok(())`. `fn end_drawing() -> Result[void, GpuError]:` does `match owns mem.take(ref mut this.pending):`, with `Some(frame): frame.present()?` and `None: pass`, then `return Ok(())`.
other_cases.settled: Compiles under LT-45 as changed. `from dev` names an earlier field whose value has a block of its own. So `dev` is never replaced after init (E2104 at any line that would replace it), and its device is changed through `this.dev` and through the frame's link (both holders, LT-46). DRP-2 ends `pending` before `dev`, so a frame that was never presented is abandoned while its device still lives. If begin_drawing is called twice, the second begin_frame gives Ok(None) (one open frame); OWN-5 then abandons the old frame and stores None.

other_cases.case: A holder overwritten, or two begins in a row: `pending = dev.begin_frame()?` in a loop while last round's frame is still held there. OWN-5 evaluates the new value first, then drops the old one.
other_cases.settled: GPU-14: while a frame is open, begin_frame gives Ok(None) and never waits for an image. So the new value is None, then the old frame is abandoned, and the next round begins a frame as usual. One round shows nothing, and nothing hangs. With `first = dev.begin_frame()?` followed by `second = dev.begin_frame()?`, `second` is None. In debug the device reports this once, naming the line that began the open frame.

other_cases.case: A frame skipped on purpose: `if scene.is_empty(): mem.drop(owns frame)`, or a `continue` or `return Ok(())` out of the frame's branch.
other_cases.settled: Abandoned, as for `?`. A present forgotten on a normal path also abandons the frame, so nothing is shown. It is not refused (that is option E).

other_cases.case: A frame given to the wrong device: `tool_view.end_frame(owns frame)` for a frame `main_view` began, or `tool_view.abandon_frame(ref mut frame)`.
other_cases.settled: This cannot be written. The frame presents itself (`frame.present()`), with no device argument, and no Device method touches a frame. Under F, which keeps today's spelling, it stops at that line after one pointer compare.

other_cases.case: A frame abandoned twice, or abandoned and then presented: a program calling the device's abandon hook, or an implementer's end_frame that forgets to take the work out of the frame.
other_cases.settled: This cannot happen. Nothing a program holds offers a hook (GPU-14). The work is one value the frame owns: present hands it to submit, and every other end of the frame ends it once (OWN-1). An implementer writes submit and a drop for its own type, and never touches std's Frame.

other_cases.case: A lost device (a GPU reset) at present or at begin_frame.
other_cases.settled: GPU-2: `frame.present()` returns Err(GpuError), and the device is then in the state an abandoned frame leaves it in. `begin_frame()` returns Err while the device is lost. `?` passes the error up, and ignoring either Result is W2190. The game loop no longer runs on silently showing nothing.

other_cases.case: A helper given both: `fn upload(ref mut dev: dyn Device, ref mut frame: Frame, mesh: Mesh)` called as `upload(ref mut dev, ref mut frame, m)`.
other_cases.settled: Compiles under LT-46 as changed. `dev` is a holder of the frame's link, so both may change the device. That call uses a copy of `upload` in which `dev` is not compiled noalias (BRW-22). Calls that pass `dev` alone keep noalias.

other_cases.case: Recording one frame on several cores: `lists = frame.command_lists(n)`, then one scoped task per list.
other_cases.settled: Compiles (GPU-13). The lists are disjoint parts of the frame, and each task changes only its own list (P16, THR-11). The tasks reach the frame where it is (verdict 164). The frame submits the recordings in list order.

other_cases.case: A window resize: `taa = gpu.History[TextureHandle].new(ref mut dev, desc, count=2)` over the old History.
other_cases.settled: GPU-8 as changed. OWN-5 makes the new History, then ends the old one, whose end destroys its two textures once the GPU has finished with them (GPU-6). Nothing leaks. A Ring works the same way (GPU-4).

other_cases.case: A texture for one frame, and an error after it: `minimap = frame.create_texture(desc)?`, then `mask = frame.create_texture(desc2)?` fails.
other_cases.settled: GPU-3 as changed. The minimap belongs to the frame and is destroyed at once with the abandoned frame, so nothing builds up from frame to frame. Made with `dev.create_texture` instead, it is a long-lived object named by a handle (the GPU handles case below).

other_cases.case: A generator holding a frame across `yield`, dropped while suspended.
other_cases.settled: CORO-7 drops it, so the frame is abandoned. While the generator is suspended the device's frame is open, so begin_frame gives Ok(None) until then. Frame is not @must_drop, because no safety guarantee rests on its drop (THR-6).

other_cases.case: `device.destroy(h)` called during a frame that is then abandoned, and a buffer written through `Ring.current(frame)` in it.
other_cases.settled: GPU-2 and GPU-6. The handle is invalid at once, and the physical destruction waits only for presented frames. The ring slot is not in flight because of the abandoned frame, so the next frame may write it with no GPU-4 panic.

other_cases.case: A panic, or process.exit, while a frame, a lock guard, a file or a scope lives.
other_cases.settled: No scope is left: no drop runs (PAN-1, STD-24), and the operating system and the driver take everything back. This is unchanged, and now stated in DRP-9.

other_cases.case: A save routine: `w = BufWriter(File.create(path)?)`, then `w.write(data)?`, then `return Ok(())`.
other_cases.settled: W2190 at the line where `w` ends (DRP-9 rule 3, STD-22). The drop's `this.flush()` is a step that can fail, and the last call that changed `w` was a write. The help gives `w.flush()?` above `return Ok(())`. With that line, a full disk reaches the caller and the drop has nothing left to write. On an error path (`w.write(data)?` failing) there is no warning: the caller is already told that the save failed.

other_cases.case: File and Socket on an early `?`.
other_cases.settled: Both are closed on every exit. Bytes a write took are with the operating system (rule 2). Closing them is not a step whose failure loses what a call accepted.

other_cases.case: GPU textures and buffers made with `dev.create_texture` before an early exit (handles are Copy, GPU-1).
other_cases.settled: A handle is a name and holds nothing, as a Pool handle or an Entity does (HND-1). Losing it leaves the object to the device: the object stays until `device.destroy(h)` or the device's end, which destroys it (GPU-6), and debug reports it (GPU-7). A texture for one frame is made through the frame instead (the per-frame texture case above). An owning handle is a question for the handle model (open risk 4).

other_cases.case: Lock guards, Scope and JobScope, ScopedArena, JoinHandle and Retained callback tokens ending on `?`.
other_cases.settled: These are DRP-9's instances and are unchanged. A guard unlocks, and changes made under it stay (DRP-6). A scope joins its tasks, which run to their end (THR-5, JOB-2). A scoped arena releases its memory after the values made in it (ARN-6, E3063). A JoinHandle detaches. A Retained token unregisters its callback once (FFI-23, verdict 62; P08's).

other_cases.case: A library transaction type: `struct Transaction` with `conn: sharedref mut Connection` and `open: bool = true`. `fn commit() owns this -> Result[void, DbError]:` does `this.conn.exec("COMMIT")?` then `this.open = false`. `fn drop():` does `if this.open: this.conn.exec("ROLLBACK").ok()`.
other_cases.settled: DRP-9 rule 2 and its finishing-call paragraph: commit is the value's own finishing call. A `?` before commit rolls back. A COMMIT that fails leaves `open` true, so the drop rolls back. A successful commit leaves nothing pending. The drop's `exec` is a call on `conn`, not one of Transaction's own methods, so rule 3 gives no warning; a rollback that fails loses nothing. In a class that keeps the connection, the field is `tx: Option[Transaction] from conn` (LT-45).

other_cases.case: An implementer whose FrameWork drop panics.
other_cases.settled: It aborts with its message (DRP-4), as any drop that panics does. The ends of std's own types never stop the program.

design.prior_art:
C++: destructors run on every scope exit. std::lock_guard unlocks. fstream closes and swallows a failed flush. std::thread's destructor calls std::terminate if the thread was not joined (option B); jthread joins instead. libpqxx's transaction aborts in its destructor unless it was committed (A). Nothing ties a frame or a command buffer to its device, so destroying the device first is found only by the Vulkan validation layer.

Rust and wgpu: Drop runs on every exit, `?` included. wgpu's `SurfaceTexture::present(self)` is a consuming method of the frame itself, and a SurfaceTexture dropped without it is discarded. That is exactly A's `frame.present()` and abandon. A CommandEncoder dropped without finish() is discarded, and a RenderPass ends its pass when dropped (GPU-13's closing of an open pass). rusqlite and sqlx roll back a Transaction dropped without commit (A). BufWriter flushes on drop and ignores the error. Rust lets a program hear that error through `#[must_use]` and `into_inner() -> Result`; rule 3's W2190 makes hearing it the default. Rust makes its ties with lifetimes (RenderPass<'a>) or with Arc counts (wgpu, and vulkano's Arc<Device>), which cost an atomic count per object. Ember's inferred link avoids that.

Vulkan and D3D12: vkAcquireNextImageKHR and vkQueuePresentKHR return VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST and VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR, and IDXGISwapChain::Present returns DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED. A present whose signature cannot fail loses these errors, hence `-> Result`. Acquiring more images than the swapchain allows, with no timeout, is invalid use, hence one open frame and `Ok(None)`. Engines record secondary command buffers (Vulkan) or command lists (D3D12) on separate threads; `frame.command_lists(n)` gives the same.

Swift: ~Copyable types end through consuming methods that write `discard self`, which is a second way to end a value. Ember's `mem.take` does the same with neither. Ada: Finalize runs on every exit. C#: TransactionScope.Dispose without Complete() rolls back (A), and Dispose may throw. Go: `defer w.Flush()` loses the error; Go's idiom is `if err := w.Flush(); err != nil`, which is the line W2190's help gives. Zig: errdefer, written by hand. Python: `with open(...)` closes the file on exit and raises if the final write fails, so the failure is heard. Ember has no exceptions, so its compiler asks for the Result-returning call instead. Vale and Austral: linear types refuse a value that its consuming call has not finished (option D).

From these Ember takes four things. From C++ and Rust, a drop on every exit. From wgpu, a frame that presents itself by a consuming method and is discarded when dropped without it. From Rust, C# and libpqxx, rolling back pending work by default. From Python, that a failed final write is never lost unseen, here by a compile-time warning since Ember has no exceptions. The tie to the device is inferred from the call that made the value (LT-1, verdict 140) and checked when compiling, at no run-time cost; none of these languages has that.
design.cost:
Ending on every exit: the compiler places the cleanup calls that C writes by hand on each error path (`goto cleanup`). A value handed over on only some paths costs one hidden flag byte and one test (OWN-3), the same as C's `if (frame) abandon(frame)`.

The frame's link: two words in the Frame (the device's address and its kind's method table, IV.9), against C's one `frame->device`. That is 8 bytes more per open frame and no time. The tie is checked when compiling. A command list's tie to its frame costs nothing. A Ring or a History holds two words each.

Present: one pointer is moved (the work handed to submit), plus the submit and present calls C makes anyway. The test at the frame's end that the work was taken is one compare per frame, folded away when present is inlined (static dispatch). The two Results per frame (begin and present) cost one branch each, as C tests its VkResult.

Abandoning a frame, which runs only on that path:
- discarding command buffers that were never submitted: a pool reset the next frame does anyway;
- giving the image back: one driver call, or keeping it for the next begin;
- resetting the frame arena: one pointer store;
- forgetting the access states the frame recorded: one store per resource it used;
- destroying the objects made through the frame: one retirement push each.
That is what a C renderer's error path does.

One open frame: one flag test per begin_frame, the same flag C keeps to avoid the same hang.

Parallel lists: nothing beyond C's secondary command buffers and the vkCmdExecuteCommands call that joins them.

LT-46's holders: a `ref mut` parameter loses noalias only in the copy of a function that is called with a link to its place; every other call keeps noalias. Rule 3's W2190 and LT-45's no-replacement check cost nothing at run time; they are compile-time checks.

BufWriter, File, lock guards, scopes, arena scopes, JoinHandle and callback tokens are unchanged, and equal to C's fflush, fclose, unlock and join at the same points.

readability.ordinary_before:
from std.gpu import Device, GpuError

fn run(ref mut dev: dyn Device, ref mut game: Game) -> Result[void, GpuError]:
    while game.running:
        game.update(1.0 / 60.0)
        started = dev.begin_frame()
        match owns started:
            Some(frame):
                minimap = dev.create_texture(game.minimap_desc())?   # today: what happens to `frame` on an error is undecided
                draw_world(ref mut frame, game)
                draw_minimap(ref mut frame, minimap)
                dev.end_frame(owns frame)                            # a lost device: nothing tells the program
                dev.destroy(minimap)                                 # skipped on an error: the texture stays until the device ends
            None:
                pass
    return Ok(())
readability.ordinary_after:
from std.gpu import Device, GpuError

fn run(ref mut dev: dyn Device, ref mut game: Game) -> Result[void, GpuError]:
    while game.running:
        game.update(1.0 / 60.0)
        started = dev.begin_frame()?                                 # a lost device is an error the caller hears
        match owns started:
            Some(frame):
                minimap = frame.create_texture(game.minimap_desc())? # the frame's: given back when it ends, on every path
                draw_world(ref mut frame, game)
                draw_minimap(ref mut frame, minimap)
                frame.present()?                                     # submits and shows; `frame` ends here
            None:
                pass
    return Ok(())
readability.note: The after is one line shorter and adds no new word. It has a `?` at the two points where a failure can now be heard. `frame.present()` is the frame's own finishing call and is shorter than `dev.end_frame(owns frame)`. `frame.create_texture` makes a texture that lives for one frame, which removes the `destroy` line. On an error at the create_texture line, the frame is abandoned and the minimap given back; nothing undefined happens and nothing builds up. A program that keeps `dev.create_texture` with `dev.destroy` still compiles. The only words a program may add are `from dev`, where one class keeps both the device and a frame (LT-45's existing spelling), and `w.flush()?` before a writer's end, which the compiler asks for (W2190). A library's finishing call uses the existing `mem.take`, not a new `discard` word.

design.compiler_does:
- Places each value's end on every exit of its block: falling off the end, `return`, `?`, `break`, `continue`, and a `with` block's exit. It also places it on an overwrite, at the end of a temporary's statement, in a suspended generator that is dropped, and with whatever owns the value (CTL-8, DRP-2, DRP-3, CORO-7). Where a value is handed over on only some paths, it keeps one hidden flag (OWN-3).
- Infers the ties with no word written. The results of `dev.begin_frame()`, `History.new(ref mut dev, ...)`, a Ring made from a device, and `frame.command_list()` point into what made them (LT-1, verdict 140). A link made from a name makes that name one of its holders (LT-46).
- Refuses a Frame, Ring or History kept past its device, and a CommandList kept past its frame (E3063). Refuses present while a list of the frame is still used. Refuses replacing a field that a `from` names (E2104).
- Compiles a `ref mut` parameter without noalias only in the copy of a function that is called with a link to its place (LT-46, BRW-22); noalias stays everywhere else.
- Works out which parts of the frame a call uses (BRW-4, BRW-10, LT-35), so a command list and the rest of the frame can be used together.
- Reads each type's `drop` body for steps that can fail: calls of the type's own methods that return a Result. It gives W2190 at an end on a path that does not leave by an error, where the last call that changed the value was not that step.
- Counts each end as a call of the drop (DRP-8). The frame's end changes the device through its link, so a frame ended inside a walk of what that end changes is refused like any other such call.
- Folds away the test at a frame's end (is the work still there?) when present is inlined.
- Applies verdict 164: Frame, Ring and History stay on their thread, and scoped tasks reach them where they are.
- The programmer writes nothing for any of this, except `from <field>` where one class keeps a provider and what it made.
design.misuse:
- Presenting a frame twice, or after mem.drop: E3040 (OWN-3).
- Keeping a Frame past its device: E3063. The help: `frame.present()?` above the line, or keep the device and the frame in one class with `pending: Option[Frame] from dev`, which compiles under LT-45 as changed.
- Replacing or handing over a field that a `from` names: E2104. The help: make another object.
- Presenting while a command list of the frame is still used: refused. The help: move present below the list's last use.
- Ignoring the Result of present or begin_frame: W2190.
- A BufWriter that ends after a write with no flush since, on a path that is not an error path: W2190, with `w.flush()?` as the help.
- `frame.drop()`: E3070 (DRP-1).
- A value made in `frame.arena()` kept past the frame: E3063 (GPU-3).
- Ending a frame inside a walk of what its end changes: E3020 (DRP-8).
- Sending a Frame, Ring or History to an unscoped thread: E7015 (verdict 164).
- Giving a frame to another device, or abandoning one through a hook: cannot be written.
- Beginning a frame while one is open: not refused, since the open frame may sit in a field. The result is Ok(None), and debug names the line that began the open frame.
- Forgetting present on a normal path: the frame is abandoned and nothing is shown. It is refused only under option E.
- A panic inside a frame stops the program at its line (PAN-1). A drop that panics aborts with its message (DRP-4).
design.verdicts:
No verdict is revisited.

- **56, kept.** A value counts as ended before its drop runs. The frame's end runs its work's drop and the device's destroy calls through the link; neither makes an owner of the frame (DRP-5).
- **57, kept and relied on.** Ending a Frame, a Ring or a History counts as a call of its drop (DRP-8), so every rule sees the changes it makes to the device.
- **58, kept.** A finishing call takes the pending work out with mem.take. Nothing ends a value without its drop, and neither forget nor `discard self` comes back.
- **69, kept.** No drop writes a `changes` word.
- **140, used.** "A method gives a result that points into its object, as every method does" gives the frame-to-device and list-to-frame ties with no word.
- **147, and FN-4.** `frame.present()` takes `owns this`, so the call writes no word, as `h.join()` does. `Frame.new(sharedref mut this, owns work)` writes `owns` before its owns argument.
- **164, applied.** Frame, Ring and History each hold a `sharedref mut` link, so none is Send or ThreadShared. GPU-13's parallel recording uses the verdict's own clause: scoped tasks reach the frame where it is.
- **ERR-5 (W2190), extended in reach, not in meaning.** An unused Result is a warning; an end's step is now one more place where a Result can go unused.
- **THR-6 (ODR-054), unchanged.** No safety guarantee rests on a Frame's drop, because the tie is checked when compiling and begin_frame copes with an open frame. So Frame is not @must_drop.
- **Verdict 11 and principles 7 and 8.** The correct `?` program is made to work, not refused (D is rejected for that reason). The tie is decided when compiling, and the abandon is the cheapest run-time act, the one C does.
- **No verdict decides today's spelling `dev.end_frame(owns frame)`.** Hardened_10 wrote it to apply verdict 147's `owns` at the call. Replacing it with `frame.present()` revisits no verdict; it is an API change for the owner, and option F keeps today's spelling.

options_for_owner.summary: One rule for every value's end (DRP-9): give back what it holds, keep what is done, and discard work that waits for the value's own finishing call. For a frame that call is `frame.present()`, and every other end abandons the frame. The frame owns its device work, so the work is submitted or abandoned exactly once.
options_for_owner.code:
fn render(ref mut dev: dyn Device, desc: TextureDesc) -> Result[void, GpuError]:
    started = dev.begin_frame()?
    match owns started:
        Some(frame):
            sky = dev.create_texture(desc)?      # an error: `frame` ends here and is abandoned
            draw_sky(ref mut frame, sky)
            frame.present()?                     # submits and shows
        None:
            pass
    return Ok(())
options_for_owner.outcome: Compiles. On the error, render returns it. Nothing is drawn this frame, and the window keeps the last frame. The image goes back to the device, the recording is discarded, and the frame's memory and the objects made through it are given back. The next begin_frame works as usual. A lost device is an Err from begin_frame or present. Keeping a frame past its device is refused when compiling (E3063); a class that keeps both says `from dev`. Another device's frame cannot be presented, because the frame presents itself. It costs what C's cleanup path costs, plus one word in the frame.

options_for_owner.summary: A Frame ended without present stops the program, as C++'s std::thread destructor calls std::terminate.

# Frame's drop: panic("a Frame ended without present")

As a rule for every resource, a transaction ended without commit would also stop the program, so `?` could not be used while any such value lives.

options_for_owner.summary: A Frame's end submits and shows what was recorded, as present does (and as BufWriter flushes).

options_for_owner.outcome: Compiles. On the error, a half-drawn frame is shown: the sky is missing for one frame, a flash. A failure of that submit (a lost device) cannot be reported from an end, so it is lost. As a rule for every resource, a transaction ended by `?` would commit half its work: silent corruption.

options_for_owner.summary: Refused when compiling unless every path hands the frame to present or to mem.drop: a linear type, as in Vale and Austral.
options_for_owner.code:
fn render(ref mut dev: dyn Device, desc: TextureDesc) -> Result[void, GpuError]:
    started = dev.begin_frame()?
    match owns started:
        Some(frame):
            match dev.create_texture(desc):
                Ok(sky):
                    draw_sky(ref mut frame, sky)
                    frame.present()?
                Err(e):
                    mem.drop(owns frame)         # every path must end it in writing
                    return Err(e)
        None:
            pass
    return Ok(())
options_for_owner.outcome: The program in A is refused at the `?` line ("`frame` may end here without present"). The program above compiles and does what A does. Every fallible call inside a frame becomes a five-line match, which is longer and harder to read, and a correct program is refused.

options_for_owner.summary: A, plus a mark the library writes once (`@ends_by(present)` on Frame). A frame that ends by its drop on any path other than `?` or a `return` of an `Err` is refused when compiling.
options_for_owner.code:
# std.gpu
@ends_by(present)
struct Frame: ...

# a program
fn render(ref mut dev: dyn Device, scene: Scene) -> Result[void, GpuError]:
    started = dev.begin_frame()?
    match owns started:
        Some(frame):
            if scene.is_empty():
                return Ok(())                    # refused: `frame` ends here without present
            sky = dev.create_texture(scene.sky)? # allowed: an error leaves, and the frame is abandoned
            draw_sky(ref mut frame, sky)
            frame.present()?
        None:
            pass
    return Ok(())
options_for_owner.outcome: The program in A compiles and behaves as under A. The `return Ok(())` line is refused: "`frame` ends on line 6 without `frame.present()`, so this frame is never shown; show it with `frame.present()?` above line 6, or skip it with `mem.drop(owns frame)`". A forgotten present is caught when compiling. The cost is a new attribute word, and an end rule that depends on how a path exits (`?` against `return`). It can be added to A later without changing A.

options_for_owner.summary: A, keeping today's spelling `dev.end_frame(owns frame)` as the finishing call. The device compares the frame's device with itself at that line and stops on a mismatch.
options_for_owner.code:
fn render(ref mut dev: dyn Device, desc: TextureDesc) -> Result[void, GpuError]:
    started = dev.begin_frame()?
    match owns started:
        Some(frame):
            sky = dev.create_texture(desc)?
            draw_sky(ref mut frame, sky)
            dev.end_frame(owns frame)?           # a frame another device began stops here
        None:

options_for_owner.outcome: Compiles and behaves as under A. `tool_view.end_frame(owns frame)` for a frame `main_view` began stops at that line: "panic at render.em:9:13: `tool_view.end_frame` was given the frame `main_view` began on line 4; end it with `main_view.end_frame(owns frame)`". It costs one pointer compare per frame. A mistake that A makes impossible to write is found only when this line runs.

recommendation.reason: A is how every resource in Ember already ends: a guard unlocks, a scope joins, a scoped arena frees, a token unregisters. It states that once, as one rule, and extends it to work that waits for a finishing call. The `?` program works. Nothing is undefined, nothing half-done is shown or committed, and the device is ready for the next frame. The frame owns its device work and presents itself, so double ends and wrong-device ends cannot be written, at no cost. A lost device is heard, and a writer's lost final write is caught when compiling. The tie to the device is inferred from the method that made the frame and checked when compiling; it is stated once, as LT-4 already states it for arenas. The other options fall short. B turns a handled error into a crash. C shows half a frame, would commit half a transaction, and loses the submit's failure. D refuses the correct program and makes every frame longer. E needs a new word and an end rule that depends on how the path exits, to catch a mistake that is visible on the first run and harmless. F keeps today's spelling, but finds a wrong-device mistake only when the line runs, where A makes it impossible to write. Checklist items 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11 and 13.

owner_short.one_line: In C++ terms: what a frame guard's destructor should do when an early return (Ember's `?`) leaves `render()` between `begin_frame()` and the frame's present. It could submit, call `std::terminate`, or roll back the way an uncommitted transaction's destructor does.
owner_short.step_table:
| step | thread | what happens | the value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | main | `started = dev.begin_frame()?` | a `Frame`: swapchain image 2 acquired, a recording open, its arena empty |
| 2 | main | `match owns started:` takes `Some(frame):` | `frame` owns that `Frame` and its device work |
| 3 | main | `sky = dev.create_texture(desc)?` fails (out of GPU memory, say) | an `Err(GpuError)` |
| 4 | main | the `?` returns that error from `render` | `frame` ends on that line without `present`, so its `drop` runs |
| 5 | main | today: `Frame` has no stated `drop`; GPU-2 covers only a frame never begun or ended twice | is image 2 still acquired? is the recording still open? does the next `begin_frame` work, hang or fail? undecided |
| 6 | main | under A: the frame is abandoned, so its work ends | recording discarded, image 2 back to the device unshown, arena freed; the window keeps the last frame; the next `begin_frame` works |
owner_short.today: Undecided. A `?` between begin_frame and end_frame leaves the acquired swapchain image and the open recording in no stated state, because Frame has no drop and GPU-2 only refuses a frame that never began or was ended twice.
owner_short.options:
A: the frame's end rolls it back (recording dropped, image back unshown, memory freed, the next frame works), by one rule for every resource's end, with no new word. The frame presents itself (`frame.present()?`), so it is submitted or abandoned exactly once.
B: the frame's end stops the program ("a Frame ended without present"), as C++'s std::thread destructor calls std::terminate.
C: the frame's end submits and shows what was recorded: a half-drawn frame on an error, and a failed submit goes unreported.
D: refused when compiling unless every path calls present or mem.drop, so no `?` while a frame lives.
E: A, plus a library mark (`@ends_by(present)`), so a frame left any way other than by an error is refused when compiling.
F: A, keeping today's `dev.end_frame(owns frame)`, which stops at the line if it is given another device's frame.
If A, these lines follow, each its own question after this one:
(1) `begin_frame` and `present` return a Result, so a lost device is heard.
(2) A `sharedref mut` link made from a name makes that name one of its holders. This is stated once in LT-46; LT-4 says it for arenas today.
(3) A class may keep a provider and a value linked to it, as in `pending: Option[Frame] from dev`; `dev` is then never replaced.
(4) A type whose drop makes a failing call of its own (BufWriter's flush), ending after a write with no flush since on a path that is not an error path, gets the unused-Result warning W2190.
(5) A frame may make objects that last one frame (`frame.create_texture`), and command lists for several threads (`frame.command_lists(n)`). History and Ring destroy what they hold when they end.
owner_short.recommendation: A. The `?` program works with no new word: nothing is shown half-drawn, nothing is undefined, and the next frame works. It is the rule every Ember resource already follows (a guard unlocks, a scope joins), and it costs what C's cleanup costs. Because the frame presents itself, a frame can never be ended twice or by the wrong device.

repairs.hole: Safety, high: `abandon_frame` on the public Device interface lets a program abandon a frame twice, or abandon it and then submit it. 'Submitted or abandoned, once' rested on each implementer's end_frame taking the work out of std's private fields.
repairs.answer: Closed by structure, with no hook. The frame owns its device work as one value of the implementer's own type (GPU-14, FrameWork): `submit() owns this` makes it real, and its drop abandons it. std's `frame.present()` hands it to submit, and every other end of the frame ends it. Once-ness follows from one owner (OWN-1). Device has no frame method a program could call, and a frame's work is reached only through its frame. This is the fix hint's owned work value, kept inside std's Frame, so programs still write `Frame` and never `owns dyn ...`.

repairs.hole: Safety, high: `tool_view.end_frame(owns frame)` accepts a frame that main_view began.
repairs.answer: Closed when compiling, at no cost. The finishing call is the frame's own, `frame.present()` (DRP-9: a finishing call is a method of the value's own type, as commit is), so there is no device argument to get wrong. This changes today's spelling, so option F keeps `dev.end_frame(owns frame)` with a one-compare stop at the line, for the owner to choose.

repairs.hole: Safety, medium: begin_frame while a frame of the same device is open is undecided, and OWN-5's order makes the design's own overwrite case do exactly that; a Vulkan host can hang.
repairs.answer: GPU-14: a device has at most one open frame, and while one is open, begin_frame gives Ok(None) and never waits. The overwrite case is corrected (other case 6): the new value is None, then the old frame is abandoned, and the next round works. It costs one flag test per begin, as in C. Debug names the line that began the open frame. A panic was not chosen: it would crash the overwrite program, whose intent (replace the frame) is met one round later.

repairs.hole: Safety, medium: the command list's kind is unstated. As a view of the whole frame it refuses ring.current(frame) and frame.arena() while recording, and refuses two lists at once.
repairs.answer: GPU-13: a list views a part of the frame of its own (`from` that part), so the rest of the frame is used as usual while the list lives (BRW-4, BRW-10, LT-35). `frame.command_lists(n)` gives n disjoint lists at once. D.1's example is unchanged and compiles.

repairs.hole: Safety, medium: a class that owns its device and keeps the pending frame has no spelling, because LT-45 needs `from <let field>` and CLS-9a forbids changing a let field.
repairs.answer: LT-45 as changed gives a general rule for every kept sharedref mut field. Such a field may say `from <field>` for an earlier field whose value has a block of its own, `let` or not. That field is then never replaced after init (E2104), its object changes through it and through the links, and DRP-2 ends the frame first. The Renderer compiles with `pending: Option[Frame] from dev` (other case 5), and E3063's help gives that line. The same rule serves an arena kept with the values made in it, and a connection kept with its transaction.

repairs.hole: Safety, medium: end_frame returns nothing, so a lost device or a failed present is lost, against rule 3.
repairs.answer: `frame.present() -> Result[void, GpuError]` and `begin_frame() -> Result[Option[Frame], GpuError]` (GPU-2), as create_texture already returns a Result. Err is a lost device; None is only a frame skipped by design. Ignoring either is W2190 (ERR-5). This goes to the owner as its own line beside the main question.

repairs.hole: Safety, medium: a BufWriter whose last write fails at drop, on a path that returns Ok, silently truncates the file.
repairs.answer: DRP-9 rule 3 as repaired. The compiler reads from the drop's body the step that can fail (a call of the type's own method that returns a Result). An end on a path that does not leave by an error, where the last call that changed the value was not that step, is W2190 at that line, with the help `w.flush()?`. With that line, a full disk reaches the caller. It is not a stop at the end, because the drop cannot know whether the program is already reporting an error; a stop would turn a handled failure into a crash, which is why B is rejected. W2190 is how Ember already keeps a Result from going unseen (ERR-5; an error under -D warnings). No new word, and the check costs nothing at run time.

repairs.hole: Engineering, medium: BRW-1 refuses the frame's link changing the device while `ref mut dev` is still used. Only LT-4's manager sentence allows it, and GPU-2 added a second per-type sentence.
repairs.answer: LT-46 as changed states it once. A sharedref mut link made from a name makes that name one of its holders, whether it is an owner or a ref mut name, and BRW-1's aloneness holds against every other name. LT-4 and GPU-2 cite this sentence. It also settles a helper given both the name and a value holding its link (other case 11): the call is allowed, and compiled without noalias in that call's copy (BRW-22). It changes BRW-1's reach, so it is an owner line; for arenas it is what LT-4 says today.

repairs.hole: Engineering, medium: the same Renderer class (LT-45 and CLS-9a); the E3063 help 'or keep the device with it' did not compile.
repairs.answer: As for the Renderer hole above: LT-45's `from <field>` for sharedref mut fields. The help now gives `pending: Option[Frame] from dev`, which compiles.

repairs.hole: Engineering, medium: `sharedref mut dyn Device` is not a form that TYP-45 or IV.9 gives.
repairs.answer: Real. It depends on P12, whose rule (1) allows every holder word before every type that can be held that way, `dyn I` included. P23 is presented after P12, and std uses no form a program cannot write. Without P12, std would need a hidden form, which this design does not take.

repairs.hole: Engineering, medium: the public abandon_frame is a second spelling of 'skip this frame', and an explicit call of what a drop does.
repairs.answer: As for the first hole: the hook is gone. `mem.drop(owns frame)`, or any exit, is the one way to skip a frame.

repairs.hole: Engineering, medium: once-ness rests on implementer code taking the work out of std's Frame.
repairs.answer: As for the first hole: the implementer writes submit and a drop for its own type, and std's present hands the work over, so there is nothing to forget. An implementer's drop that panics aborts (DRP-4), as any drop does. The implementer's contracts sit beside robust buffer access (GPU-12).

repairs.hole: Engineering, medium: History and Ring own GPU resources but give nothing back, so every window resize leaks two textures.
repairs.answer: GPU-8 and GPU-4 as changed. Each is made from the device and holds a link made from it (LT-46), and its end destroys what it holds (GPU-6's deferred destruction). See the window resize case in other_cases.

repairs.hole: Engineering, medium: Copy handles leave GPU objects alive past an early exit, so an allocation that keeps failing in a frame loop leaks one texture per frame.
repairs.answer: The repeated leak is closed. A texture for one frame is made through the frame, `frame.create_texture(desc)`; it belongs to the frame and is given back on every end (GPU-3 as changed; rule 1). A long-lived handle stays a name that holds nothing (GPU-1), as HND-1's Pool handles and ECS entities are. It is destroyed by `destroy` or by the device's end, and reported in debug. An owning handle type was weighed and not taken here. Its end must reach the device, so it would be tied to the device and could not be kept in a class that does not hold the device (LT-45), which is what handles exist to avoid. It is the handle model's own question (open risk 4).

repairs.hole: Engineering, medium: OWN-5's order (the new value first, then the old one dropped) begins frame N+1 while N is still open, which can hang.
repairs.answer: As for the open-frame hole above: begin_frame gives Ok(None) while a frame is open, so the round is skipped and N is abandoned. Other case 6 names OWN-5's order.

repairs.hole: Engineering, medium: verdict 164 makes Frame and its command list non-Send, so one core records the whole scene.
repairs.answer: GPU-13: `frame.command_lists(n)` gives disjoint lists. Scoped tasks reach the frame where it is (verdict 164's own clause), and each task changes only its own list (THR-11, P16). Verdict 164 and the tie are kept. Moving a whole frame to an unscoped thread stays refused, just as a Device itself is not Send today.

repairs.hole: Engineering, medium: rule 3 and STD-22 make silence the stated behaviour for a BufWriter's failed final write.
repairs.answer: As for the BufWriter hole above: W2190 at the line where the writer ends, read from the drop's body, with `w.flush()?` as the help. No new word.

repairs.answer: GPU-2 now says that what the frame's GPU work would have written keeps its contents, while what the CPU wrote during the frame stays. frames_in_flight, Ring and History count only presented frames.
